text:
alice: Heads up — after the routing-policy canary landed we're seeing a small but steady spike in fncall schema validation errors when requests get routed to the cheaper fallback variant. Support is getting a couple tickets.

ben: how big is "small"? link to a log sample?

alice: ~0.9% of fncalls in the canary slice over the past 45m. here's the last failing tool payload (redacted):
```
tool_response: {
  \"action\": \"create_order\",
  \"payload\": \"<xml>...</xml>\"
}
schema expected: { order_id: string, items: array, total: number }
error: missing required key 'order_id'; got unexpected key 'payload'
```

dinesh: this reads like the fallback model doesn't have the tool binding/schema adapter. routing sent to fallback that returns freeform. Are we surfacing the raw tool output up the stack or do we wrap? That affects both validation and billing.

carol: telemetry gap: we don't tag schema rejects with the route_id or fallback_variant. propose a metric: `fncall.validation.rejects.count{env,route_id,fallback_variant}` and a histogram for token_billed_on_reject. Also add a sample id to the trace so console can fetch the exact request/response.

alice: console UX ask: can we show "fncall reject rate by route" in Model Health and a quick link to the sample trace? right now SRE has to ask infra to pull logs.

ben: quick question — current billing semantics: do we bill tokens on strict rejects? customers keep pinging support about being billed for invalid outputs.

dinesh: current behavior (FYI): tokens are billed as usual because the serving path completes with a model response even if validation fails. we don't refund automatically. that's why this is a support pain.

carol: rollout idea: while the canary is active, add an instrumentation flag that logs `route_decision` + `validation_result` to the fncall trace. small change but gives us per-route signals. I'll prototype.

alice: policy question — should fallback responses count against quota/usage? two user-facing options: 1) bill always (current, simpler), 2) do not bill when strict schema rejects (complex, touches billing). internal compromise: bill but mark for automated credits when a validation audit confirms systemic issues.

ben: for short-term mitigation: can we make the routing policy preference explicit in the console — e.g., per-route toggle: "allow_fallbacks" or "strict_no_fallback"? customers could set strict for mission-critical flows.

dinesh: infra note: allowing automatic retry to primary before exposing fallback might reduce customer-visible rejects. e.g., if fallback chosen due to transient capacity, one quick retry to primary could succeed. we should instrument retries separately.

carol: proposal for telemetry + console UX:
- metric: `fncall.validation.reject_rate` by route and variant
- tag: `fallback_reason` (capacity|cost-policy|version-mismatch)
- sample link + last_successful_variant in the trace
- expose drop-in filter in console to show "requests that hit fallback" and "requests that failed validation"

alice: agree. also add a small banner in Console's rollout UI showing "This routing policy may route to variants without tool bindings — expect fncall rejects" during canary.

deploy-bot: rollout-canary/44 applied to routing policy `cost-optimizer` (slice=5%). fallback=enabled, fallback_variant=opt-lite-v2

ben: I'll open a telemetry PR (prom/ship) and a console ticket for the toggle + banner. assigning myself and @dinesh for infra changes, @carol for metrics.

alice: thanks. can we also add a short-term QA job to generate mismatched-tool responses and assert console surfaces samples? saves us a messy support backlog.

dinesh: +1. I'll add a chaos test in the routing simulator to randomly swap bindings.

carol: will prototype the metric tags and a Grafana panel; then hand off to @ben for console integration.

ben: cool. will update thread when PRs are up. :thumbsup:
